This matches the PI's T2a override, which used the post-trimming Table 1 counts (36,778, not 36,783).

[Design straddle, codes 4/5] Severity = No, sibling = No and N = 214 are confirmed. SIGH-ADS was compared descriptively, not modeled, and the Mood Disorder group is defined by diagnosis alone. But every effect estimate the paper reports is crude (chi-square/CMH). The logistic model adjusting for preterm birth, race and age is reported only as P values ('results not shown'), and the Methods describe the crude group comparison as the primary analysis. Code 4 depends on reading Amendment 2.2's 'fully adjusted, if adjusted' as also governing study_type; read strictly as 'primary analysis', it would be code 5. I don't disagree, but the PI should set one rule and apply it to both ref 111 and ref 142.

Codes confirmed. Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT. The primary analysis compares response rates in the 36-woman ITT sample (17 sertraline, 19 placebo). 38 entered the placebo lead-in and 2 were removed before randomization. Severity = NA and sibling = No are correct for an RCT.

concern: sample_size_n: use 71931, not 93436. study_type, severity = No and sibling = No are confirmed. The case-control analysis precedes code 7 in the decision order, and the review only generated hypotheses. Severity is No because the authors had no data on epilepsy type or seizure frequency. 93,436 is the whole case-control dataset: all 5 case groups plus both control groups (it is the denominator in 516/93,436 AED-exposed). The raters themselves name the main estimate as the spina bifida OR of 2.6 vs no AED, using non-chromosomal controls. That model contains 2,048 spina bifida cases + 69,883 control-group-1 registrations = 71,931 (Table 4). The true analytic N is somewhat smaller and not reported. The registry-adjusted model dropped registries with no carbamazepine exposure, and registrations exposed to other AEDs drop out of the CBZ-vs-no-AED contrast. So treat 71,931 as an upper bound.
flag_reason: [Disagree - N; design straddle, codes 4/7] (1) N, as above. If the PI treats all five malformation groups x two control groups as one co-primary analysis, 93,436 could stand. That needs a PI convention, kept consistent with the single-headline-contrast rule already applied to T2a and ref 110. (2) The design straddles case-control and review/pooled analysis. PubMed indexes it as a Systematic Review, the title and abstract present both parts, and the Conclusions cite the review's pooled 3.3% major-malformation prevalence alongside the case-control OR. Code 4 is correct under the decision order, but the dual design is worth recording.

Codes confirmed. Purely descriptive prevalence and trend study, with the 585,615 qualifying deliveries as the denominator for every prevalence estimate. No effect estimate, no adjustment, no sibling analysis. Minor: there is no treated-vs-untreated effect comparison, so severity = NA would also be defensible under the protocol's NA rule. The raters' No matches the round-1 majority for descriptive studies.

[Design straddle, codes 3/5] Severity = Yes rests on the model, not only on an author claim: Models II and III enter SIGH-ADS and Mania Rating Scale symptom scores (Table 2). Sibling = No and N = 197 dyads are also confirmed. The fully adjusted model's dyad count isn't reported; its denominator df drop from 253 to 234. But the only positive finding in the abstract and Conclusions (Motor Quality, P = .0441) comes from unadjusted Model I. It became non-significant once the symptom scores were added (P = .0529). Model III also used postbirth symptom scores, which may act as mediators rather than baseline confounders. So code 3 describes the fully adjusted models, not the paper's headline claim. Apply the same rule as for ref 111.
